title: Claim, reason, example, and meet Rebut
summary: Learn the four rules for talking to an AI, then debate a robot named Rebut for the first time.

steps.title: The AI is a sparring partner
steps.body:
Today you meet an AI for the first time: a debate partner named Rebut. Four rules before you start.

Rebut is a practice partner, not an oracle. It is there to help you practice arguing, not to hand you the one true answer.

Rebut can be wrong. Check what it says instead of believing it just because it answered fast and sounded sure.

Never tell Rebut your full name, your school, your address, or anything private about yourself. Talk about the ideas, not about exactly who you are or where you live.

Rebut is a robot; it will say so if you ask it directly. Go ahead and ask it, right at the start, whether it is a robot.

steps.title: Claim, reason, example
steps.body:
A strong argument has three parts. A claim: the one sentence you actually believe. A reason: why you believe it. An example: something real that backs the reason up, so it is not just a feeling.

Try it on something small before the debate. 'Ice cream is the best dessert' is a claim. 'Because it is cold and sweet at the same time' is the reason. 'Like on a hot day when nothing else feels as good' is the example.

The question of the week is: should anyone be able to tell you what to do? Think about who tells you what to do and why, a parent, a teacher, a coach, and whether that is ever a good thing. Keep your answer in mind, since claim, reason, example is exactly what you need in a minute, when you debate Rebut.

steps.title: Record it
steps.prompt: Record part of the debate, or record yourself afterward explaining your strongest claim, reason and example.
